project.title: Fold
project.medium: Puzzle game for iPhone and the browser, in progress – Swift, SwiftUI, JavaScript, pixel art
project.content:
A puzzle game about folding a sheet of paper over itself – work in progress. You can play it right here in the browser.

You play a paper boat on a sheet, and the goal is a sheet of coloured paper. Fold the sheet and the top layer wins: holes become windows onto the layer below, pins stop a layer from lifting. Each level awards up to three pinwheels for using few folds, and the islands – leaf, wave, ember, sky – each have their own colours, map and soundtrack. The look is deliberately its own: one-bit pixel art in ink and paper, a pixel font and chunky buttons instead of the style of this site.

It is a native iPhone app written in SwiftUI, with a browser version that follows it.

caseStudy.role: Solo project – game design, level design, pixel art, music, Swift
caseStudy.challenge: Make a puzzle where one simple move – folding the sheet over itself – stays interesting for a hundred levels, and where every level can really be solved.

decisions.title: Few rules that combine
decisions.text: The top layer wins, holes are windows and pins block lifting. Each rule is easy to read on its own; the puzzles come from how they meet.

decisions.title: Levels proven, not hoped for
decisions.text: A script checks that every level is solvable and searches for new ones, and a rating pass sorts them by difficulty, so the order teaches the game step by step.

decisions.title: Native, with its own look
decisions.text: I built it as a real SwiftUI app instead of a web wrapper, with its own pixel font, themed islands and soundtracks composed by script – coherent in itself, not a copy of my portfolio.

caseStudy.result: A playable iPhone game with several islands of levels, an intro and endings, tested on my own phone.
